why: The student correctly flattens the nested else into an else-if chain, preserving all three branches, their order and their prints, showing a working model of if/else-if; the only fault is changing > to >=, which makes x = 0 print "pos" instead of "zero" (and leaves the final else unreachable). That is a single slip in an otherwise rule-correct restructuring, so it is L2 with an error rather than L0, and since the new code is not behaviour-preserving it cannot be L4.
